title: Fast and Efficient Scaling for Microservices with SurgeGuard
problem: Existing resource management mechanisms for microservices suffer from high latency in detecting Quality of Service violations and fail to allocate resources effectively under varying load conditions, resulting in over-allocation and significant QoS violation events.
motivation: Rapid QoS violation detection and effective resource allocation are critical for reducing both total cost of ownership and SLO violation magnitude in microservice applications.
method: SurgeGuard is a decentralized system (one without a central coordinator) that manages computing resources for independent services called microservices. It works by understanding two things: how much slower each service can run before falling below its performance standards (called latency slack), and how the services communicate with each other. Using this knowledge, it rapidly detects when service quality will drop and intelligently allocates additional computing power during traffic spikes and network slowdowns.
key_novelty: By understanding how microservices communicate and their available timing margins, a system can rapidly detect quality failures and adjust resources without centralized control.
contributions: Decentralized resource controller (SurgeGuard) for microservice QoS management
61.1% reduction in combined violation magnitude and duration vs Parties/Caladan
93.7% reduction in violation duration compared to existing algorithms
8% reduction in resource requirements compared to Parties baseline
